title: ValidateJWTSVID verifies against the local ephemeral key only and ignores the trust bundle store entirely
description:
persona-grpc/src/service.rs:219-228:

    let pub_key_der = self.signer.public_key_der();
    let decoding_key = DecodingKey::from_ec_der(pub_key_der);
    ...
    decode::<serde_json::Value>(&req.svid, &decoding_key, &validation)

The service holds self.bundles: Arc<TrustBundleStore> (service.rs:18) and never reads it in this RPC. Validation therefore succeeds only for tokens signed by this process own in-memory keypair.

Two concrete triggers:

(1) Daemon restart. SvidSigner::new() (persona-core/src/signer.rs:172-185) generates a fresh ephemeral P-256 keypair on every start, and personad/src/main.rs:31-32 calls it unconditionally. A JWT-SVID has a 300-second TTL (signer.rs:212). Restart personad -- systemd Restart=on-failure with RestartSec=5 is configured in persona/src/main.rs:46-47 -- and every unexpired token issued by the previous process is rejected by ValidateJWTSVID as an invalid signature, while its exp says it is still valid. A consumer holding a 4-minute-old token gets a confusing "JWT validation failed" instead of an expiry.

(2) Federation. TrustBundleStore exists specifically to hold other trust domains keys (trust_bundle.rs:32-33: "Populated at daemon startup from the local CA key and any federated sources"), and FetchJWTBundles serves them. But a JWT-SVID issued by any other personad or federated domain whose bundle is present in the store is still rejected, because its key is never consulted. The trust bundle is published to consumers and then not honoured by the daemon own validation path.

There is also no issuer/trust-domain check: nothing verifies that the tokens spiffe_id claim (service.rs:230-239) belongs to the trust domain of the key that signed it.

Fix direction: resolve the verification key from self.bundles by the tokens trust domain (falling back to the local signer for the local domain), which also requires the JWKS in the bundle to be populated -- see the separate empty-JWKS issue.
close_reason: Fixed together in e3940ad. The bundle publishes a real one-key JWKS keyed by the trust domain's SPIFFE ID and no X.509 authority (empty is proto-permitted; a SEC1 point in an ASN.1 DER field was not). ValidateJWTSVID resolves the bundle and selects by kid with no fallback to the local key. A third-party verifier using only the published JWKS and the token, via python stdlib plus openssl, is part of the suite and was observed failing against the unfixed code first.
